ZIMRA FDMS Fiscal Gateway

Built a full REST integration with the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority FDMS. It signs tax receipts cryptographically, validates invoices in real time, and manages daily opening and closing routines automatically.

ZRA SmartInvoice (Zambia)

Built the integration for Zambian operations to meet ZRA SmartInvoice rules. It handles invoice formatting, status polling, and offline queues when the network drops.

Odoo v17 → v18 Migration

Upgraded customized client instances from Odoo 17 to 18. Updated deprecated ORM methods, fixed QWeb report templates, and verified that every database table migrated cleanly.

PostgreSQL & Reporting Tuning

Fixed database locks and slow queries on busy systems by cleaning up queries and adding the right indexes. Also built multi-currency financial reports and balance sheets in QWeb.

Beyond the Code

Chess, Books & How I Think

Software is what I do for work, but I spend plenty of time thinking about other things.

I'm an introvert, so I do my best work in quiet stretches of time. When I'm not coding or troubleshooting deployments, you'll usually find me playing chess, solving a sudoku puzzle, or reading.

I play a lot of chess online. I especially like Chess960 because it randomizes the starting pieces. You can't rely on memorized opening lines, so you have to figure out the board from scratch every game. It requires patience and thinking through consequences before making a move — which feels very similar to working with production databases.

“You have power over your mind - not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.” — Marcus Aurelius

I read quite a bit, mostly philosophy and science fiction. Stoics like Marcus Aurelius and writers like Alan Watts have had a big influence on how I stay calm when things break. I also journal every day to clear my head, review mistakes, and organize my thoughts before starting work.

When I'm working, I almost always have music on. My playlist jumps around between hip-hop (J. Cole, Kendrick Lamar), rock (Linkin Park), Hans Zimmer movie scores, and simple lofi beats when I need to focus on a bug.
